thread:
ops_jane: Heads up — customer-reported latency spike. p99 for /v1/generate jumped ~40% starting at 12:03 UTC after today's canary runtime rollout (v2.3.1). Can anyone pick this up?
ben_runtime: I see it on Grafana too, p95 also moved but p99 is where it hurts. Canary cohort shows spike aligned with traffic switch. link: https://grafana.internal/r/abc123
maya_sre: Tagging for oncall. @alex_oncall can you tail the canary hosts and confirm queueing?
alex_oncall: On it. tailing logs now — seeing increased request queued durations and a few 503s from sidecar. sample log: 
```
2026-03-17T12:04:19Z host-12 runtime: request queued=120ms process=45ms kvcache_hit=false
2026-03-17T12:04:20Z host-12 sidecar: upstream 503 code=503 msg=overloaded
```
ben_runtime: Interesting — kvcache_hit=false is higher for these requests. Did the rollout change cache warming behavior? v2.3.1 added a lazy-kv-prefetch flag we flipped on in canary.
ops_jane: Customer impact: degraded experience for long prompts, multiple retries causing higher cost. They want mitigation ASAP.
maya_sre: Quick triage checklist: 1) confirm cohort sampling (we did), 2) check kernel selector change, 3) isolate variant. Ben, can you run a bisect on kernel selection if applicable?
ben_runtime: Running a synthetic replay against canary and baseline now (using stressproxy). Command: `./stressproxy run --profile=prompt-heavy --target=canary-hosts --samples=5000`
ci-bot: Synthetic replay started on canary (job 7743). ETA ~6m.
alex_oncall: Also seeing increase in small-batch runs falling back to slow attention kernel on GPU due to changed sequence length histogram. That could explain tail.
ben_runtime: Replay results: p99_canary=680ms, p99_baseline=470ms. Delta ~210ms. Flamegraph points to attention kernel path switching around token 1024.
ops_jane: Can we hotfix by reverting lazy-kv-prefetch or force old kernel selector?
ben_runtime: I can flip lazy-kv-prefetch off in canary hosts (config rollout). Doing config patch now. `rkctl config set runtime.lazy_kv_prefetch=false --scope=cohort-canary`
ci-bot: Config change applied to 20/20 canary hosts.
ben_runtime: Monitoring... initial signs p99 dropping in canary to ~510ms. Still slightly above baseline but much better.
maya_sre: Good. Recommend holding rollback until we confirm stability. Also create a postmortem ticket and capture exact traffic cohort.
alex_oncall: Will keep sampling for 15m and check for regressions on cold-start cohorts.
ops_jane: Logged customer update: we're investigating and applied a temporary config rollback; will follow up in 30m.
ben_runtime: Root cause hypothesis: lazy prefetch changed cache population timing which increased KV miss rate for long sequences, causing fallback to slow attention kernel and queueing. Bisect note: kernel selector threshold crossed because sequence histogram in canary slightly shifted upward.
maya_sre: Action items: 1) Ben - revert default for next deploy and add A/B flagging for kernel selector thresholds. 2) Alex - continuous sampling script to compare kvcache_hit rate across cohorts. 3) Ops - notify affected customers in 1:1 threads.
ops_jane: Assigning and moving to a short incident channel for follow-ups. Thanks all :thumbsup:
ci-bot: Incident created: INC-2026-0317-09 (link: https://incidents.internal/INC-2026-0317-09)
